note: Disclosure guard. A curator authors sensitivity on a column only through [[errata.column]] is_sensitive (or a documented-blank matrix's answer_facts); no curation surface can lower a raw Unika claim, and the replaced tests' checked-sensitivity precedence branch was deleted as unreachable (maintainer decision on #1267). This case pins the disclosure invariant that remains: the authored flag reaches variables.is_sensitive in both directions, and a flag the curator did not write is never read as non-sensitive. It also pins the other facts a declaration supplies: its name, its definition (as the description) and its classification reference reach the built state, and the delivered column the declaration is anchored on keeps its own facts. Expected literals: new-on 1 from test_source_effect_routing.py::test_column_declaration_preserves_only_supplied_flags_and_periods (addition.fields.sensitivity == value_field(True) for is_sensitive=True); new-off 0 from test_checked_sensitivity_overrides_raw_and_conditional_support_claims (formed.variable.is_sensitive is False) and test_authored_sensitivity_on_added_occurrence_overrides_raw_claims (flags.sensitivity.value is False); held 0 from test_source_effect_routing.py::test_steward_storage_type_and_flags_preserve_curated_identifier (a steward-held entry without the key: effect.fields.sensitivity == value_field(False)); the no-flag variable is absent and reported unresolved_flag because the routing test asserts an undeclared flag stays None and an unknown flag withholds the variable (test_source_formation_facts.py). no-id is the routing test's own setup: is_sensitive supplied, is_identifier not (addition.fields.identifier is None), so it is withheld as unresolved_flag too. The old test's entry carried is_identifier=False outside its declared_flags; a TOML entry cannot, because the compile derives the declared flags from the keys written (curation_compile.py, `row.model_fields_set`), so the key is omitted here. Because an unknown flag withholds the state, the omitted flag and the supplied prose sit on two entries (no-id and new-on), where the old test read both off one intermediate addition. new-on's name 'Authored name', description 'Authored description' and its declared classification 'FIX' are the old test's values (addition.fields.name, .description, .classification_declared); the declaration names the book by short name, so it binds the book whose short_name is FIX (slug fix). The delivered column A keeps its own name and definition, the var_row defaults GenericVar and 'A generic family label' of this source spec, as the old test asserts its originals keep their fields and carry no correction. The withheld_alias_dependency row is the one code test_search_alias_distinguishes_withheld_dependencies_from_missing_conversion asserts for an alias of a withheld variable, and its case_id is the alias entry's locator in this curation file. The flagged columns raise no issue: both replaced test_source_effects.py tests assert `result.diagnostics == ()` for an authored flag, and so does the routing test.
fails_if: `scb_errata.convert_column_entry` stops taking `sensitivity` from `entry.is_sensitive` (for example `sensitivity=value_field(False)`), so new-on is built non-sensitive; or it sets a flag for a non-steward entry whose key is absent from `declared_flags`, so no-flag or no-id is built and its unresolved_flag issue disappears; or it drops `classification_declared`, `name` or `description` from the added occurrence, so new-on binds no book or loses its authored prose; or it writes the declaration's fields onto the delivered record it is anchored on, so A's name or definition changes
